scope: Leakage-safe VACE data export from accepted metric flower simulation
summary: The accepted 660-frame physical rollout was converted into 12 training clips and four source-frame-disjoint validation clips with explicit depth, centerline, contact, target, and identity controls.
evidence: Dataset validation reports train_clips=12, validation_clips=4, and train_validation_frame_overlap=0.
Every clip is hash-bound to the accepted simulation, metric camera, and persistent stem artifacts.
The control review shows calibrated inverse depth, robot and flower edges, the named centerline, and the active contact marker.
The frozen manifest authorizes only BSD-3-Clause G1 and Apache-2.0 Sharpa-derived procedural frames; no Pexels frame enters training.
lessons: Physical state should be compiled into training controls before appearance adaptation rather than asking a diffusion model to infer contact from pixels.
limitations: All clips share one simulated rollout and validation is not an independent scene or seed.
The exported data alone does not show that a VACE adapter improves a real replacement.
next_actions: Run a bounded trainer smoke and compare the adapted checkpoint with zero-shot generation on all four held-out windows.
